title: When does a director's personal liability actually pierce the corporate veil
p1: Many people believe a company structure always protects directors from personal risk. But there are situations where that protection can disappear, and a director may find their own assets exposed.
p2: A common misconception is that every business mistake can lead to personal liability. Usually, directors are protected because the company is a separate legal entity. The surprise is that courts may look beyond the company if it is being misused, such as when there is fraud, deliberate wrongdoing, or the company is treated like a personal wallet instead of a separate business.
p3: Piercing the corporate veil is not about punishing normal business decisions. It is about holding individuals accountable when the company structure is used as a shield for improper conduct. Keeping proper records, separating personal and company finances, and following legal duties can help preserve that protection.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a case where a director was personally responsible despite having a company behind them?
